name: MonarchButtonGroup
title: ButtonGroup
summary: Related standard Buttons shown as one control: joined into one shape with a hairline between them, or kept apart with a small gap, and exposed to VoiceOver as one labelled group.
whenToUse: For two to four related actions of equal weight, such as Previous and Next or zoom in and out.
whenNotToUse: For choosing one option from a set, use a segmented Picker. For buttons that stay on or off, use Toggle with the toggle button style. For one main action with alternatives, use a single button and a Menu.
api: MonarchButtonGroup.init(_ label: String? = nil, axis: Axis = .horizontal, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, isAttached: Bool = true, fullWidth: Bool = false, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)

options.name: label
options.description: What the buttons have in common, read by VoiceOver. Already localised.

options.name: variant
options.description: primary, secondary, ghost or danger, for every button.

options.name: size
options.description: sm, md or lg, for every button.

options.name: isAttached
options.description: Joins the buttons into one shape. When false they keep an 8-point gap.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Fills the available width. In a row the buttons share it.

options.name: content
options.description: The buttons: standard Button, ShareLink or other views that take a button style.

states.name: resting
states.description: One rounded shape. Secondary has a border; every variant has a hairline between neighbours.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Only the pressed button changes its fill; not animated when Reduce Motion is on.

states.name: disabled
states.description: A button disabled with disabled(_:) takes the disabled fill and text colour; the others are unchanged.

states.name: not attached
states.description: Each button is drawn alone with the Monarch button style.

appearance: The fills, text colours and pressed colours are those of the button variant in every theme. The line between two filled buttons (primary, danger) is the surface colour; for secondary it is the default border colour and for ghost the subtle border colour.
platformNotes: The web group joins any child and lets each child keep its own variant; here the group sets one variant and size for all its buttons, because a SwiftUI container cannot restyle each child separately on iOS 17. A view that sets its own button style, including MonarchButton, keeps it and is not joined, so use standard Buttons inside. In a row the joined shape is 32 to 40 points high inside a 44-point touch target; in a column every button is at least 44 points high because the buttons touch. Android uses the same name and parameters.
accessibility: The group is an accessibility container with the given label, so VoiceOver reads the label when focus enters it.
Every button stays a standard Button: its own element, trait, label and disabled state.
Every joined button is at least 44 points wide; in a row the touch target is 44 points high around the visible shape, in a column the visible button is at least 44 points high.
Labels scale with Dynamic Type and wrap; the joined shape grows to the tallest button.
The joined shape follows the buttons in right-to-left layouts.
The press transition is not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: A view inside the group that sets its own button style, such as MonarchButton, is drawn alone and not joined.
One button gives a single rounded shape with no line. No buttons draw nothing.
With long titles in a row, the buttons wrap their text and all take the height of the tallest.
The label is optional; without one the buttons are read without a group name.
